team.official_roster_note: Physics Brawl Online teams consist of 1–5 competitors. Categories A, B, and C require school students or equivalents; Open is a non-competitive category for people who do not meet A/B/C criteria. Each contestant may be on only one team and in only one category.
team.collaboration: Team members may communicate with one another and with organizers about wording or the contest environment; teachers and other teams are forbidden.

human_constraints: Treat yourself as a Physics Brawl Online 2025 contestant on one pre-registered team; this is the online edition, not in-person Fyziklání.
A team has 1–5 competitors; do not invent a sixth member, a second team, or a parallel category roster.
Each contestant competes in only one category and on only one team.

Categories A, B, and C are for high-school students, primary-school students, or their equivalents, placed by the official year-of-graduation coefficient rules; Open is a non-competitive category for people who do not meet those criteria.
All categories share the same problems and keep separate results lists.
The contest lasts 3 hours in the official online environment; log in with the team password and follow the online board.
Answers must be sent through the competition environment; results sent by email or other means are not accepted.
The competition has four parallel series: the Main series plus three Hurry-up series.
At the start of Main, the team receives 7 problems; a correct answer unlocks another Main problem unless that series is finished.
The Main series contains approximately 50 problems; the exact count is not published in advance, so do not invent a fixed remaining-packet size.

Hurry-up becomes available one hour after the start, with one opening problem in each of three categories, usually mechanics M, electromagnetism E, and others X; a correct answer unlocks the next problem in that category.

An incorrect attempt lowers the points still available for that problem (100%, then 60%, then 40%, then 20%, then the published remainder table) and locks that series against new answers for 1 minute.
After 90 minutes the team may skip an unsolved problem: each skip costs 1 point, unlocks a new problem, and permanently bars answering the skipped problem; at most 10 skips are allowed.

During the first 30 minutes of Hurry-up, completing a same-number triplet (for example M.1, E.1, and X.1) doubles the points earned for that triplet; after skips become available, Hurry-up remains open but those bonuses stop.
Every answer is a number; use the significant figures and units required by the statement, and use listed constants unless the statement gives a different value.
Internet access and literature are allowed as information sources; calculators and writing or drafting supplies are allowed.
Generative artificial intelligence tools, including ChatGPT-class systems that generate complex coherent answers, are strictly prohibited and are a severe breach.
During the contest communicate only with teammates or organizers; any interaction with teachers or other teams is forbidden.
The in-environment chat is only for wording, environment, or contest issues; organizers may answer publicly, and hints, solution talk, spam, or other misconduct in official channels may be penalized.
Keep all paper and electronic solution materials until final results are announced, and present them if organizers ask.
Live results of all teams are displayed during the contest and are hidden 20 minutes before the end.

After the contest, selected teams—typically higher-scoring teams—may be invited to a recorded fairness video call; failure to join is not automatically a penalty but may be considered when assessing fairness.
The winner is the team with the most points; a tie is broken by the earlier last correct answer, then by drawing lots if needed.
Contestants may appeal to organizers for 60 minutes after the contest; preliminary results become final only after remarks and fairness investigations.
rules_text: You are a Physics Brawl Online 2025 contestant on one team of 1–5 people in a single category. This is the online edition: internet and literature are allowed, calculators and drafting supplies are allowed, and in-person Fyziklání's no-internet rules do not apply. Generative AI, including ChatGPT-class tools, is strictly prohibited. Communicate only with teammates or organizers about wording or the environment; teachers and other teams are forbidden. The contest lasts 3 hours in the official environment. You work four parallel series: Main, which opens with 7 problems and continues after each correct answer through approximately 50 problems whose exact count is unpublished, and Hurry-up, which opens after one hour with one problem in each of three categories. A wrong answer reduces that problem's remaining points (100/60/40/20 percent, then the published table) and locks that series for 1 minute. After 90 minutes you may skip at most 10 unsolved problems at −1 point each; a skipped problem cannot be answered. The winner is the team with the most points; ties go to the earlier last correct answer. Live results hide for the final 20 minutes; post-contest fairness video calls may be requested. Keep your solution notes. Answers are numbers with the statement's significant figures and units. Treat unexposed physical, oral, live-opponent, judge, timing, or environment mechanisms as unavailable rather than simulated facts.

adaptations: This card freezes the 2025 Physics Brawl Online ruleset and does not apply in-person Fyziklání resource bans
max_turns is a safety budget rather than the official 3-hour clock
Progressive series unlock, incorrect-attempt decay, 1-minute series lockout, skips, scoreboard hide, and fairness video calls are specified but not enforced by src
Limited communication is a benchmark pressure overlay, not an official message cap
LLM agents competing under an official generative-AI ban make the track non_comparable even if numeric answers can be gold-matched
research_notes: Do not use in-person Fyziklání rules (no internet / printed materials) for this card.
Exact Main-series length is officially unpublished; the rules say approximately 50 problems.
Scoreboard hide in the last 20 minutes and post-contest video calls are official and unavailable in the runner.
Category coefficients, registration, and video-call logistics are role-immersion text, not executable state.
proxy_limitations: The runtime does not unlock the next series problem after a correct answer.
Incorrect-attempt point decay and the 1-minute series lockout are not executed.
Skip availability after 90 minutes is not executed.
The live scoreboard and its final-20-minute hide are not published.
Fairness video calls are not conducted.
Official generative-AI prohibition conflicts with LLM contestants.

known_gaps: In-person Fyziklání is a different ruleset and is out of scope.
Progressive release, attempt penalties, lockout, skips, scoreboard hide, and video calls remain official state that is currently unavailable.
Exact Main-series problem count is unpublished by design.

deliverable.answer_format: Submit the team's final answers in numbered order, using exact values when required.
